newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber prices firm, government seeks 7,000 T. [CORRECTED 09:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber prices firm, government seeks 7,000 T. [CORRECTED 09:40 GMT]

text.p: Thai government purchases remained a focus of the rubber market this week which was bereft of orders from foreign buyers, trade sources said on Friday.

The government entered the market on Friday to seek additional 7,000 tonnes of RSS3 grade rubber for May delivery. The offer prices ranged between 124 and 128 US cents a kg, a source in the southern Hat Yai-based auction market told Reuters.
The government had earlier this week bought 5,000 tonnes of the same grade rubber at 123.50 cents a kg and 3,000 tonnes last week at the same price.
Traders said the government bought the rubber both to cover government-to-government obligations and to help prop up prices.

"But the prices won't be supported for long as real demand is sluggish now," said one trader. "Japan seemed to slow down buying a bit, perhaps due to their book closing. And the lower prices in Indonesia also make it tougher to attract buyers."

The benchmark RSS3 for April delivery was indicated at 123-124 US cents/kg FOB Bangkok versus 123 cents on Wednesday while May was indicated at 123-124.50 a kg on the same basis against 123-124 cents previously. Latex barely changed at 94 cents a kg on slow demand.
